node: Energy supplier-risk intelligence, procurement analytics, inspection, certification, and supply-chain assurance
summary: Expanded the node into four US-listed mappings: one reference/anchor distributor and three underfollowed or shadow candidates in supplier-risk data, grid/energy testing and certification, and industrial asset-integrity inspection. The key Serenity hypothesis is that if energy supply-chain risk becomes structural, value may accrue not only to equipment OEMs but also to firms that help utilities, EPCs, developers, and industrial buyers qualify suppliers, secure constrained parts, certify grid-connected equipment, and monitor critical assets. Evidence is strongest for WCC, DNB, and ULS as direct node fits; MG is a smaller speculative-shadow candidate because its asset-integrity and inspection exposure is relevant but less clearly tied to procurement or supplier assurance.
